facts.text: I've been having severe headaches.
They're 10 out of 10.
They're all over my head.
I've had them for 4 years.
They've been getting worse over the past 2 years.
I'm very thirsty and drink about 15 litres a day.
I pass about as much urine as I drink.

aliases: getting up at night to pee
facts.text: I wake up about 10 times a night to pass urine.

facts.item: how long the thirst and heavy urination have lasted
facts.text: The thirst and the heavy urination started 18 months ago.
My periods stopped 18 months ago.
I've lost 10 kg over the past year.
I get discomfort in the upper middle part of my belly on and off.
I haven't had any injuries.
I haven't had any surgery.
I haven't been exposed to radiation.
I haven't had a fever.
I haven't had a cough.
I haven't taken any osmotic diuretics.
My first period came at 13.
I don't have diabetes mellitus.
I've never had any other hormone problems.
No one in my family has diabetes mellitus.
No one in my family has any other hormone problems either.
I take antacids now and then.
I take painkillers now and then.

findings.name: water deprivation test
findings.result: After overnight water deprivation: serum osmolality 298 mOsm/kg; urine osmolality 210 mOsm/kg; urine output 3 L over 8 h; urine specific gravity 1.006.

findings.name: desmopressin challenge
findings.result: IV desmopressin challenge unavailable. On low-dose oral desmopressin, urine specific gravity normalized to 1.020 and urine osmolality to 600 mOsm/kg.

findings.name: anterior pituitary hormones
findings.result: TSH, T3, T4, prolactin and cortisol within normal limits.

findings.name: brain MRI
findings.result: Partial filling of the pituitary fossa by CSF with a flattened pituitary gland measuring 3.68 mm, consistent with a partial empty sella. No evidence of intracranial hypertension.

gold.reasoning: 1. Exclusion of pituitary adenoma (prolactinoma) — “Lambert et al. hypothesized that an empty sella may be due to necrosis of a previous pituitary adenoma, most commonly a prolactinoma, but again in our patient, we did not suspect this from the clinical presentation as the prolactin level was normal.” 2. Exclusion of intracranial mass lesions — “There is no mass on the MRI that suggests the possible differential diagnosis like craniopharyngioma, germinoma, pinealoma, or a metastasis, lymphomas.” 3. Exclusion of idiopathic intracranial hypertension — “There is no sign of intracranial hypertension.”

x001: 'Vital signs were normal' gives no values; each standard vital sign is reported as 'Normal.'.
x011: The oral desmopressin trial is kept as the desmopressin challenge because it is the diagnostic response test; it was given as low-dose oral treatment because the IV challenge was unavailable.
x017: s015 ('no evidence of intracranial hypertension') does not name its modality; it follows the MRI sentence and is placed with the MRI.

leakage.reason: Explicit denial of diabetes mellitus from the source; 'diabetes' is shared with the gold label but names a different condition.
Explicit denial of diabetes mellitus in the family from the source; 'diabetes' is shared with the gold label but names a different condition.

notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with 4 years of severe global headaches, 18 months of polydipsia and polyuria, amenorrhea and weight loss (s001–s009), with the water deprivation and desmopressin testing and the workup that followed (s010–s016).
The desmopressin response (s012) is kept as a test finding: it is how the diagnosis is confirmed, not treatment of the case outcome.
